title: Extreme CO Isotopologue Line Ratios in ULIRGS: Evidence for a Top-heavy IMF
question: Why are 13CO/C18O J=1-0 ratios extremely low in ULIRGs and a post-merger galaxy, and do they indicate a top-heavy IMF?

data.bands: Band 6 calibration uncertainties quoted (as stated in table caption)

what.value: Infrared luminosity of NGC 2623 (and ULIRG IR luminosities)

evidence.quote: NGC 2623 is a post-merger galaxy with L$_{\rm IR}$ = 10$^{11.6}$ L$_{\odot}$ (cite: Armus2009)

recipe.method: tclean with Briggs weighting robust 0.5, channel widths 20 km/s (12CO) and 35 km/s (C18O, 13CO), matched cell/uvtaper/uvrange, smoothed to a common beam

recipe.goal: Make moment maps and integrated fluxes
recipe.method: Integrated intensity maps with 3 sigma threshold, primary beam corrected; fluxes from an aperture covering all detected C18O and 13CO emission
Convert moment maps from Jy/beam km/s to K km/s then ratio with immath

not_stated_but_needed: Which ALMA project maps to which galaxy
Cell size, image size, uvtaper and uvrange values used for matching
Final common beam per galaxy and primary beam details
Conversion to brightness temperature details and S/N cut for ratio maps
Meaning of the 3-sigma moment-map threshold (per channel or integrated)
score_reason: Data public and CASA recipe partly given, but many imaging parameters and the project-target mapping are missing.
rediscovery_reason: Public data, a simple imaging recipe, and numeric line ratios, though some settings are missing.
